title: Vinton County Siders August 21 indictment update with protected-minor redaction

data.research_question: What changed in the Vinton County Siders case on August 21, 2026, and how should the linked indictment information be normalized without identifying protected minors?
data.method: Use the Ohio Attorney General-origin August 21 indictment announcement as the authority for current adult charge counts and investigation chronology; use the supplied Law&Crime Crime Fix report as a secondary lead and cross-check; preserve the August 18 report only as historical pre-indictment provenance; name adult defendants only; suppress all protected-minor identities and re-identifying details.
classification_rules: Treat all indictments and charges as allegations pending adjudication.
Use adult defendant names only. Never create or resolve child/minor victim person records.
When a victim handle is necessary, use anonymous non-identity-bearing labels such as Minor Victim A and never map them to real identities.

Do not store victim names, initials, aliases, dates of birth, exact ages, kinship details, schools, medical providers, placement information, phone numbers, email addresses, social accounts, photographs, exact residences, or unique descriptors.
If a source exposes a protected identity, do not copy that identity into the dataset.
Retain aggregate victim counts only when necessary to accurately represent an official charging or procedural statement.
Treat the August 18 potential-charge report as historical provenance superseded for current posture by the August 21 indictments.
Do not infer a count of distinct acts from counts charged in the alternative.

findings.finding: Gary Siders Jr. and Elizabeth Siders were each indicted on two F3 sexual-battery counts and two F3 unlawful-sexual-conduct-with-a-minor counts.
Gary Siders Jr., Elizabeth Siders, and Christina Siders were each indicted on 19 child-endangerment counts; Gary Siders Sr. was indicted on 16.
The official-origin announcement says some child-endangerment counts are charged in the alternative.
The August 18 report that additional charges were under consideration is no longer the current procedural posture after the August 21 indictments.
